title: Product/market analysis of a marketplace of plugins for popular CMS
description:
I need to analyze a marketplace of plugins for popular CMS. 

The analysis aims to find 5+ categories of plugins where we can see relatively high demand but poor-quality supply. To do this, you will need to consider factors such as rating, the number of 1-star-marks, buggy products, and the lack of recent maintenance despite recent downloads, a ratio of marks to downloads, anything else that you can prove useful and find insights there. 

This task is not about a straightforward implementation of a specific request, it is consulting and creating an analytical approach to help me achieve my business goal: find a promising niche in the marketplace.

What data do I have for plugins: 
- 40000 plugins at all
- Title, URL, Description
- Author name and link
- Version of CMS, the current version of a plugin, PHP versions, etc
- Active installations, Total number of all-time downloads, and downloads per last week
- Count of opened/resolved support tickets
- Rating, amount of 1-star-marks, 2-stars, …, 5-stars
- Tags - each plugin has ~3.9 tags (we have 16000 unique tags). Plugins with 100K+ downloads have ~4.5 tags on average. 
- For plugins with 100K+ downloads, I took their tags (3200 tags) and calculated amount of common plugins for each possible pair of tags.
- There are ~2200 plugins with more than 100K downloads

Project structure

I propose dividing this task into 2 parts: classification/clusterization and finding promising clusters.

1. Clusterization

Currently, there are no categories in the dataset. I would like to combine all these tags into categories. I expect to have 100-200 categories. 
You can use my “common plugins” table or you can do it your way. These categories should group plugins with similar features and use cases together. 

NOTE: Tags for tags-pairs in common_plugins were taken from tags that have plugins with 100K+ downloads. But plugins for common_plugins were calculated within all plugins.
Deliverable here is a table of plugins-to-category mapping/association. Let me know if you think that tags-to-category mapping will be more suitable here.

2. Analyzing categories

As told, analyze the categories needed to identify those that have relatively high demand but poor supply. By poor supply, I mean lower marks than similar categories have, buggy products, and no recent maintenance despite recent downloads. But I expect that you can propose additional/other metrics for finding an “unsatisfying supply”.

Some objectives: 
- I am interested in categories where the top 4-6 plugins have more than 100K downloads each
- I would like to avoid categories with defined monopolists (more than 70% of downloads in a category belong to the top-1 plugin; top-1 has more than x3 downloads compared with the next most popular plugin in a category)
- Deliverable here is a list of categories with relatively high demand and poor supply, as well as data-driven proof of dissatisfaction that these categories bring to users. Include comparing these categories with common marketplace trends or with similar categories.

I will provide a 200-plugins CSV example and a sample of the “common_plugins” table in the chat when you text me. 

I am looking for a creative problem solver to join me in this challenge. I can't wait to see how you'll approach it, apply now!
